quotes.text: Think of Copilot as a reflection engine. Its intelligence begins and ends with the quality of your schema.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Condenses the episode's core thesis that Copilot output quality is bounded by schema quality.

quotes.text: This is the medallion myth, the idea that having layers automatically delivers purity. Layers are only as truthful as the discipline within them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Challenges the assumption that bronze, silver and gold layers guarantee clean data on their own.

quotes.text: The semantic model in Fabric tells Copilot what your data means, not just what it's called. It's the dictionary that translates column labels into business logic.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear, practical definition of why the semantic model matters for AI answers.

quotes.text: Notice the interplay. Data instructions define the facts. Agent instructions define the voice. Together they form Copilot's ethical code.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the split between data source instructions and agent instructions in one memorable line.

quotes.text: Instructions constrain language, they can't invent truth. That's why tuning is a closed loop. Architecture defines reliability, semantics define meaning, and instructions define obedience.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the layered model of architecture, semantics and instructions behind trustworthy AI.

chapters.title: Teaching Copilot to tell the truth

takeaways: Copilot in Fabric does not validate facts; it mirrors the quality, gaps and inconsistencies of your schema and metadata.
Clean medallion layers and a well-defined semantic model with consistent measures, synonyms and calculation groups are the foundation for accurate AI answers.
Centralized data source and agent instructions, example queries, certified datasets and regular truth audits keep Copilot reliable over time.
hook: Copilot in Microsoft Fabric confidently produces wrong numbers when your data model is inconsistent. This episode is for data engineers and BI teams who want to trace those hallucinations back to medallion layers, missing semantics and weak governance. You learn how to rebuild the model and instructions so Copilot answers become accurate and explainable.
